newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-ZOELLER APOLOGIZES FOR OFFENSIVE REMARKS ABOUT TIGER.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ZOELLER APOLOGIZES FOR OFFENSIVE REMARKS ABOUT TIGER.

text.p: PGA Tour veteran Fuzzy Zoeller issued an apology for offensive remarks he made about Tiger Woods during the 21-year-old sensation's historic run to the Masters championship earlier this month.

Zoeller, known as joker on the tour who sometimes ventures beyond the boundries of good taste, suggested that reporters urge Woods not to order fried chicken and collard greens at next year's Masters Champions Dinner.
"My comments were not intended to be racially derogatory and I apologise for the fact that they were misconstrued in that fashion," Zoeller said in a statement issued by his agent Monday.

Zoeller made the comments in an interview during the Masters as Woods was busy obliterating many of Augusta National's records en route to becoming the event's youngest winner and the first black player ever to win one of golf's major championships. The interview was broadcast Sunday during CNN's "Pro Golf Weekly" show.

According to a CNN transcript, Zoeller said that when Woods gets to the interview area: "You pat him on the back and say congratulations and enjoy it, and tell him not to serve fried chicken next year ... or collard greens or whatever the hell they serve."

One of the many Masters traditions calls for the defending champion to select the menu for the following year's Champions Dinner. The reference to "they" and foods associated with negative stereotypes of poor southern blacks was sure to be found offensive, even if Zoeller was only trying to be funny.
"I've been on the tour for 23 years and anybody who knows me knows that I am a jokester," Zoeller said.
"It's too bad that something I said in jest was turned into something it's not, but I didn't mean anything by it and I'm sorry if I offended anybody," Zoeller continued.
"If Tiger is offended by it, I apologise to him too."
